events.credibility_reason: Single-author Zenodo-only deposit 15 days old, posted a day after the repository's first commit; proof PDF unread; the Lean upper bound is stated conditionally on an exclusion hypothesis whose discharge for n=5,6 was not confirmed, and the README says the formalisation predates revisions. No specific error identified.

why: The statement asks e(l_1^d)<=2d for every d, so single dimensions (d=3, d=4, and Gallinger's d=5,6) are cases, and the n log n bounds are bounds. Gallinger is a case, unreviewed (a Lean build is not digestion, F7), and doubtful rather than not_credible: it is very new, and there is no error, only an unconfirmed conditional hypothesis. Ge-Xu-Zhou's p=1 bound is of the same order as Alon-Pudlak and the record could not establish any improvement, so it is none rather than bound. Swanepoel, Chalmers and Xiong concern Kusner's l_p (p≠1) n+1 claim, which this statement does not ask about, and Lin concerns l_1 sums of Euclidean spaces, so all four are variants. Their AI roles are still recorded from their own quotes: Chalmers is assisted, since the model implemented the search that produced the configuration, and Xiong is generated, since the construction was found by the model.
doubts: Close calls: Ge-Xu-Zhou (none vs bound) turns on whether its l_1 bound improves Alon-Pudlak, which the record leaves unresolved. Gallinger's Lean exclusion hypothesis may not be discharged for n=5,6, and the PDF was not read, so its AI disclosure is unknown. The Chalmers and Xiong AI quotes come from WebFetch summaries, not checked page text.
